notes: Low, medium, and high values were specified around literature-reported animal-level prevalence (~20% with lower bounds of 3–5%) and herd-level prevalence (>50% in many European countries), using Nielsen and Toft (2009) as an empirical anchor.

Scenario values were chosen to reflect the wide variation in herd-level prevalence observed across European systems, ranging from near-eradication to endemic conditions, as documented by Scharnböck et al. (2018).

Within-herd values were based on seroprevalence estimates from endemic herds, typically 25–35% with wide variation (Nielsen, 2013), while herd-level values were informed by global prevalence estimates showing low to moderate infection levels across production systems (Gutema et al., 2019).
